newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA WITHOUT KEY MEN AGAINST GIANT-KILLERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA WITHOUT KEY MEN AGAINST GIANT-KILLERS.

text.p: Barcelona will face second-division giant-killers Las Palmas in Wednesday's Spanish Cup semifinal in Gran Canaria with four first-choice players missing on international duty.
With a daunting nine points separating Barcelona from league-leaders Real Madrid, the two-leg tie is vital in coach Bobby Robson's bid to salvage something from the season.
"If we go there with a complacent attitude that would be dangerous," said Robson.

The former England coach will have to find replacements for Gheorghe Popescu, who will be playing for Romania, and three Portuguese internationals -- goalkeeper Vitor Baia, Fernando Couto and Luis Figo, who will also be absent on World Cup duty.
Substitute Carlos Busquets will take over between the posts, despite having made an appalling mistake that cost his side a goal the last time Baia missed a game.
Barcelona face a Las Palmas side that has already knocked out Valencia and Espanyol.
But the tie could provide a breathing space for Robson's team, who had to overcome Real and Atletico Madrid in previous rounds.
Robson sought to play down speculation about Brazilian striker Ronaldo, voted world player of the year, who said on Monday he might leave Barcelona at the end of the season.
"I'm quite sure that Ronaldo will have his mind on the three competitions we are playing in," said Robson.
But the former England coach had harsher words for another Brazilian, midfielder Giovanni, who has also talked of leaving.
"If his agent wants to take Giovanni back to Brazil, my advice to the club is that they should ask for the money," said Robson.
